item.title: [7.0] MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Memory-native evolution requires making memory an intrinsic capability of foundation models, enabling them to continuously accumulate and utilize information. To this end, we introduce MemT-1.0, a new architecture of memory foundation models that internalize memory as part of model computation. Building on Metis, MemT-1.0 employs Gated DeltaNet-2 with a stable token-level memory update...

WHY IT MATTERS

MemT-1.0 introduces a notable architecture for memory-native foundation models using Gated DeltaNet-2 and Mixture-of-Storage, presenting a potential alternative to traditional RAG and parametric memory limitations.

item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. Typically, these 2D-based approaches perform scene generation in a 2D latent space, which introduces two fundamental issues: (i) representing 3D scenes via 2D views leads to significant representation redundancy, and (ii) latent space rooted in 2D inherently limits the spatial consistency of the...

WHY IT MATTERS

This paper introduces a direct 3D latent space approach for scene generation using diffusion transformers, offering a notable technical shift away from redundant 2D multi-view pipelines.

item.description:

General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes.
